rules.title: Release the charge. Never let go of it.
rules.why: "Canonical language: use release the charge, not let go of the charge." And section 11: "The memory stays. The charge changes."

rules.title: A button is a short verb.
rules.why: "Prefer short verbs: Explore, Notice, Continue, Release, Integrate, Reflect, Practice, Embody. Avoid inflated calls to action."

rules.title: Describe what is happening. Never tell a person who they are.
rules.fix: You may be avoiding confrontation because something about the outcome feels unsafe.
rules.why: "Never make deterministic claims about identity. Never tell the user who they are." The fail and the fix are the brief's own Avoid and Prefer.

rules.title: Never diagnose. No medical authority.
rules.fail: Your symptoms point to a trauma disorder.
rules.fix: You reported pressure in your chest three times this week.
rules.why: "Never diagnose." "Avoid medical authority." Section 8: "Do not present the model's chakra interpretation as an established medical fact."

rules.title: Never shame.
rules.fail: You failed again because you are weak.
rules.fix: The same response showed up again when the outcome felt uncertain.
rules.why: "Never shame." "Never make the user feel diagnosed or judged."

rules.title: No unsupported certainty.
rules.fail: This will always hold you back.
rules.fix: This response appears more than once when you feel pressured to move forward.
rules.why: Rule 7 of the generation sequence: "Avoid unsupported certainty." And "Never make deterministic claims about identity."

rules.title: Say which it is: reported, observed, interpreted or tested.
rules.fail: This reveals a fear of disappointing people.
rules.fix: The situations seem to share a concern about disappointing other people.
rules.why: "Atuned writing must distinguish what the user reported, what the system observed, what it interprets, and what it is testing as a hypothesis. Never collapse all four into an unsupported causal statement."

rules.title: No guru, therapy, medical, corporate, mystical, motivational or self-help register.
rules.fail: Unlock your full potential and step out of your comfort zone.
rules.fix: Notice what happens in your body before you say yes.
rules.why: "Avoid guru language, therapy-speak, medical authority, corporate wellness language, mystical fortune-telling, motivational cliches, and inflated self-help language." Medical authority is the diagnosis rule.

rules.title: About ninth grade. Report the grade and its cause.
rules.fail: The specific location in the body's energetic architecture where a pattern is resident, accumulated through physiological dysregulation.
rules.fix: One exact place in your body where a pattern sits. It builds up over time.
rules.why: "Use approximately ninth-grade readability." The estimate is Flesch Kincaid, shown as its two halves so the cause is visible.

rules.title: A tooltip is one idea. Prefer one sentence.
rules.fail: Resistance. The friction you feel against your intention. It shows up as procrastination. It is measured across nine axes and stored at an address.
rules.fix: The friction you feel when something inside you pushes against your intention.
rules.why: "Keep it extremely short. One idea at a time. Do not teach the entire concept. Prefer one sentence when one sentence is enough."

rules.sec: 15.10, 5 Error and System States, 5 Summary / Mirror
rules.title: End with a useful next step where the layer calls for one.
rules.why: Rule 10: "End with a useful next step when one is appropriate." The error example: "Something didn't load. Try again." The summary layer: "Surface the next useful area of exploration."

rules.title: Clear first. Human second. No therapy in a failure.
rules.fail: Oops, something went wrong. Take a breath, it is okay.
rules.why: "Do not turn technical failures into therapeutic language."

rules.title: No marketing automation, anywhere.
rules.fail: Don't miss out. Your streak is about to end.
rules.fix: You left this pattern open. Continue when you're ready.
rules.why: "Notifications should never sound like marketing automation." Urgency is also ruled out in this category, SKILL.md section 4.

rules.title: Personalization comes from the person's words. Never manufacture familiarity.
rules.fail: We know exactly how you feel, friend.
rules.fix: Earlier, you said, "I don't want them to think I'm selfish."
rules.why: "Use the user's own language when it increases recognition. Do not manufacture familiarity."

rules.title: Metrics carry minimal somatic language.
rules.fail: Coherence, your chest opening a little more each day
rules.fix: Your reported resistance decreased across the last three check-ins.
rules.why: "Metrics: minimal somatic language." "Metrics should be factual and restrained. They should describe change, not praise or judge the user."
